significance.root_decision: The conjecture is false at n = 3 over every field of characteristic 0. The counterexample is a transposed Poisson 3-Lie algebra M₃ given by an explicit multiplication and bracket table, extended to polynomials in one variable t, with the derivation D = d/dt; the 4-ary operation μ built from D and the bracket fails the generalized Jacobi (Filippov) identity, with an explicit nonzero defect. The idea is that D = d/dt on the polynomial extension turns the Filippov defect of μ into a polynomial identity (a 'strong condition' whose first argument is itself a bracket) that would have to hold in the base algebra, and the table is chosen so that this degree-seven specialization is nonzero. Huang, Chen, Chen and Ding proved the construction for strong transposed Poisson n-Lie algebras, and Mashurov showed by a free-algebra computation that the strong condition can fail, without producing a counterexample to the construction. Lean states the conjecture with the bracket as a function with multilinearity and skew-symmetry hypotheses, over any field of characteristic 0, and proves its negation.
significance.caveat: The signed universal conjecture fails at n = 3; the Lean theorem covers fields of characteristic 0 (including ℚ and ℂ). The restriction to a 59-dimensional example and the extension to positive characteristic other than two are written arguments outside Lean. The witness is nonunital and infinite-dimensional (the conjecture requires neither); the result does not settle the unital case or other arities. The unsigned printing of the formula fails trivially and is not a separate result. The journal version (Comm. Algebra, doi 10.1080/00927872.2026.2689550) could not be read; arXiv v3 predates its acceptance, and the November 2026 version of the Beites–Ferreira–Kaygorodov survey still lists the question as open. Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (two rounds; not routine 0.67).
